- Add `oh harness <list|install|status>` so installing an agent harness stops requiring a full image rebuild. Adding one of the four optional harnesses previously meant knowing that `harness.yaml` carries an `install:` section, knowing the key is `install.grok_build` while the doc slug is `grok-build` and the build arg is `INSTALL_GROK_BUILD`, uncommenting a line by hand in a file whose vendored awk parser accepts a two-space indent and nothing else, and then running `make destroy && make sandbox` — several minutes, and it destroys the container — for what is a one-package operation. Nothing in the CLI helped: there was no way to ask which harnesses exist, which are enabled, or which are actually present. `install` does **both halves**, deliberately: it persists `install.<key>: true` so the choice survives the next build, **then** installs into the already-running container through the `ExecutionTarget` contract (`status()` / `exec()`, never a direct `docker exec` spawn and never a `kind` check). Live-only was rejected because a container recreate silently loses the CLI; flag-only is the rebuild pain being removed. `--persist-only` and `--no-persist` are the escape hatches and conflict with each other. The command **never** rebuilds or restarts the sandbox: an absent or stopped container is the normal not-yet-started case, so it persists, prints the `oh sandbox` hint, exits 0, and issues zero `docker exec` calls; a failing installer keeps the persisted flag and says so, because the flag is still correct for the next build. The catalog is a bundled TS module (`.oh/cli/src/lib/harnesses/catalog.ts`) rather than a data file under `.oh/` — an installed binary has no readable `.oh/` payload, which is why `resolveInitSource`/`bundledPayloadExists` exist — and rather than the docs, which are **already drifted** (`.oh/docs/harnesses/claude-code.md` says `pnpm add -g`, the Dockerfile runs `npm install -g`). `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is the ground truth for every install argv including the `0.2.39` grok-build pin, and a drift test asserts per entry that the build arg is in the Dockerfile, the key is in `harness-config.sh`'s `envmap` mapped to that same arg, the key ships in `harness.yaml.example`, and every pinned version appears verbatim in the Dockerfile. Per-harness install user is carried explicitly because it is not cosmetic: deepagents and pi run as `sandbox` (`UV_TOOL_DIR`/`UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR` live under `/home/sandbox`, and pi installs under the sandbox user's npm prefix so `pi update` needs no sudo). `.oh/scripts/harness-config.sh` stays **read-only by design** — no `set` mode was added and its grammar is not re-implemented in TS; the new `.oh/cli/src/lib/harness-yaml.ts` writer uncomments the template line **in place**, preserving its trailing build-arg comment and the file's line count, rather than appending a duplicate key the parser would read last-wins. `seedHarnessYaml`, `assertInRoot`, and `configuredContainerName` were extracted from `commands/lifecycle.ts` and shared rather than copied, following the `lib/execution/runner.ts` precedent. `install.agent_browser` sits in the same section but is not a harness and is excluded by an explicit assertion. 74 new tests: mkdtemp fixtures and injected runner fakes only, with the one real-subprocess exception being a round-trip that proves the TS writer emits something the real awk parser reads back as `true` in `get` mode and `INSTALL_<KEY>=true` in `env` mode. The Dockerfile build-arg contract, `docker-compose.sh`, and the rebuild path are untouched — this is additive.
